newsitem.title: CROATIA: Pliva hits all-time-high on Zagreb bourse.
newsitem.headline: Pliva hits all-time-high on Zagreb bourse.

text.p: Leading drugs concern Pliva hit an all-time high in an active market on Friday and dealers said they foresaw further growth.
"Pliva has sold some 8,000 shares so far and the price ranged between 550 and 560 kuna," Davor Relja of Faktor brokerage told Reuters. The previous high was 552 kuna.
He said its price was close to Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) which rose to $17.3 from $17.25 in London in the morning.
"This certainly points to further growth," he said, without giving any concrete reason for the price rise.
By contrast Zagrebacka Banka saw no transactions by 1000 GMT after breaking its own all-time high yesterday. Dealers said the bank's surge had been prompted by the strong dollar.

Relja said this was probably due to expensive and modest offer at 2,345 kuna, which overshot the London price. The bank's GDRs in London slid to $36.175 from $36.25 at the open. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
